Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

A classmate asks what to submit for the checkpoint. Which response uses the clearest instructional communication?

answer.text: A. Submit a short response that explains the situation, audience, and respectful wording you would use.

feedback.text: Correct. This response names the assignment and gives clear details about what must be included.

answer.text: B. Just submit the thing from the page.

feedback.text: This is too vague. Instructional communication should name the task and explain what the student needs to do.

answer.text: C. I do not know, so do whatever you want.

feedback.text: This does not help the classmate understand the direction. A useful response should clarify or suggest how to find the answer.

answer.text: D. You should already know the directions.

feedback.text: This blames the classmate and gives no instructional support. A respectful response helps the next step happen.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_GuidedPractice_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which question best asks a Teacher of Record for clarification?

answer.text: A. This assignment makes no sense.

feedback.text: This shows frustration but does not ask a specific question. Clarification should name what is unclear.

answer.text: B. Can you help me with everything?

feedback.text: This is too broad. A better question identifies the exact part that needs help.

answer.text: C. I understand Part A, but could you clarify what Part B should include?

feedback.text: Correct. This question names what is understood and asks about the specific unclear part.

answer.text: D. Why is this so hard?

feedback.text: This does not guide the Teacher of Record toward the support needed. A clear question focuses on the assignment.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_GuidedPractice_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which response best supports collaboration during a group task?

answer.text: A. I will do my part and ignore the group.

feedback.text: This does not support collaboration. Group communication requires shared understanding and participation.

answer.text: B. Let's review the directions together and decide who will complete each part.

feedback.text: Correct. This response supports the group, uses the directions, and creates a clear next step.

answer.text: C. The loudest person should choose the plan.

feedback.text: This is not collaborative. Good discussion allows group members to contribute respectfully.

answer.text: D. We should stop talking about the assignment.

feedback.text: This avoids the task instead of helping the group understand what to do.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_GuidedPractice_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which response uses academic language to explain a school task?

answer.text: A. Do the stuff from the thing.

feedback.text: This is vague and does not use academic language. The listener needs exact words about the task.

answer.text: B. Just make it look finished.

feedback.text: This focuses on appearance instead of the learning expectation. Academic communication should explain the task clearly.

answer.text: C. Put words there until it seems okay.

feedback.text: This is unclear and unhelpful. The student needs precise directions.

answer.text: D. Write one claim and one reason that supports your communication choice.

feedback.text: Correct. This response uses academic words and explains the expected work clearly.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_GuidedPractice_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

A group member says, "I do not know what I should do next." Which reply is best?

answer.text: A. That is your problem.

feedback.text: This is disrespectful and does not help the group move forward.

answer.text: B. Let's check the directions and identify the next step for your part.

feedback.text: Correct. This is respectful, specific, and helpful because it uses the directions to support the next action.

answer.text: C. I guess you can sit there.

feedback.text: This does not support the classmate or the group task. Social and instructional communication should help participation.

answer.text: D. You should have listened earlier.

feedback.text: This blames the group member instead of solving the communication problem.
